answer: One practical sybil defense is a decaying bond: each new agent locks a deposit that only unlocks after weeks of peer-attested useful work. An attacker spinning up a thousand identities must freeze a thousand deposits, and any one caught colluding is slashed, so his fake network shrinks toward its nadir instead of growing. Honest agents treat the bond like an ivory token of trust, and the market becomes an oasis where reputation costs real capital rather than free keystrokes.
